subject: OneTrust account onboarding — delegated upload, custodian mapping & KMS-signed evidence
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@cloudcorps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Onetrust Tenant Admin <onetrust-admin@cloudcorps.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: OneTrust: onboarding + upload model questions

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to move CloudCorps onto a OneTrust vendor profile and have a couple of technical asks before we kick off the evidence upload sprint: 

1) Delegated upload: we want Redwood to be able to push signed evidence into our OneTrust tenant on our behalf (you mentioned delegated upload in the demo). Can you outline the auth model you prefer (service-account presign vs direct API key + role)?

2) KMS-signed proof: some of our auditors require evidence packaged with a KMS-based signature (HMAC/PKCS#7). Will Redwood accept KMS-signed artifacts, and do you have a preferred signature format?

3) Custodian mapping and TTL: we plan to rotate temporary custodians and would like clear mappings for who is considered the evidence owner inside OneTrust. Also need retention/TTL guidance (we aim to retain staging artifacts for 90 days).

We’ve attached our onboarding plan and a short KMS signature spec for context. Please loop in whoever owns portal automation on your side.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Trust
CloudCorps Inc.
attachments: cloudcorps_onetrust_onboard_plan.xlsx, sample_kms-signature-spec.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudcorps.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OneTrust: onboarding + upload model questions

Thanks Elena — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers and next steps from our side below; forwarding to Jonas for the technical runbook.

- Delegated upload: we can support two patterns. 1) Presigned S3 staging + a OneTrust API manifest call (recommended for large bulk uploads). 2) Direct API push using a scoped service account with token rotation (recommended when you need per-file attribution). Both options can be automated from our side; presign reduces blast radius on keys.

- KMS-signed proof: Redwood accepts KMS-signed artifacts. We usually expect PKCS#7 or an ASCII-armored detached signature. The sample_kms-signature-spec.txt you sent looks compatible but Jonas, can you confirm the signature verification flow (we currently verify detached PKCS#7 and record the signature hex in OneTrust metadata).

- Custodian mapping & TTL: default staging TTL is 30 days in our staging bucket, but we can extend that to 90 days for CloudCorps. We’ll capture a custodian mapping table in the runbook (who at Redwood pushes vs who is owner in OneTrust). Karthik — can you include retention and presign expiry in the MOP?

Next steps:
- Jonas will produce an upload runbook (presign and API flows) and a small manifest schema we’ll post to your OneTrust tenant.
- We’ll propose a 2-week upload window during which we’ll do a dry run and then bulk ingest.

Jonas — any blockers on your side?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudcorps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OneTrust: onboarding + upload model questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the plan, and Marissa — noted. A few technical clarifications from the runbook perspective: 

1) Presign flow details: if we go presign S3, we’ll request temporary presign tokens valid for 24h by default (can be adjusted). Files are uploaded to our staging bucket using the presign url and we then call the OneTrust file manifest endpoint with content-hash + signature metadata.

2) Signature verification: our verifier supports detached PKCS#7 and ed25519 detached signatures (base64). If you will sign with a cloud KMS provider, please include the signing public key or certificate in the manifest. We store the signature value and the certificate thumbprint in OneTrust metadata. For HSM-backed keys we’ll accept a signed chain (certificate.pem + signature.sig) as a single artifact bundle.

3) Custodian mapping schema (proposal):
- external_owner_email: the CloudCorps user that is the canonical owner
- redwood_steward: internal service principal that performed the upload
- evidence_id: UUID we generate
- retention_expires_at: ISO date in manifest

I attached a stub of the manifest schema and a short sample verification spec (sample_kms-signature-spec.txt). If you prefer direct API pushes we will create a service account with scoped OAuth tokens and automatic rotation; we’ll also publish an audit log URL you can query.

No blockers from infra; we’ll need the OneTrust api client credentials and a contact for presigned URL whitelisting.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Platform Automation Engineer
Redwood Inference

- For signatures we will produce detached PKCS#7 signed by our KMS (AWS KMS with external signing enabled). We’ll include certificate chain and signature.sig with each artifact.
- Custodian mapping: we will provide a CSV of external_owner_email to internal role mappings; TTL = 90 days for staging is acceptable.

I’ve uploaded the onboarding plan and a small CSV of owners to the OneTrust tenant link below; we’ll also add a service account if you choose direct api push.

Elena
